operators.name: adaptive_avg_pool1d_transpose
semantics: Computes adaptive average pooling over the channel dimension after transposing input from [B, C, W] to [B, W, C].
Equivalent to torch.transpose(x, 1, 2) followed by torch.nn.functional.adaptive_avg_pool1d with output_size.
For each batch b and width w, output[b, w, o] = mean over c in input[b, c, w] for c in adaptive pooling interval for output index o.
When C is divisible by output_size, each output element averages exactly C/output_size consecutive input channels.
Uses stable accumulation and integer boundaries exactly as PyTorch adaptive_avg_pool1d, including non-divisible cases if called with other shapes.
Returns a new CUDA tensor with shape [B, W, output_size], dtype torch.float32.
Transposes the input tensor from shape [B, C, W] to [B, W, C] using torch.transpose.
Returns a view with stride [C*W, 1, C] for contiguous input; but the contract allows strided input.
In debug_forward, this checkpoint must be the transposed tensor matching reference shape [256, 4096, 1024] and stride [4194304, 1, 4096].
Applies AdaptiveAvgPool1d(output_size=512) along the last dimension of the transposed tensor [B, W, C].
Produces output shape [B, W, output_size] with dtype float32.
The output has stride [W*output_size, 1, W] for the given shape; actual stride [2097152, 1, 4096].
In debug_forward, this checkpoint must match reference shape [256, 4096, 512].
Returns the adaptive average pooled tensor.
Final output shape [256, 4096, 512], dtype float32, device cuda.
